scoring_rules.reverse_scoring_formula: reverse_scored_value = 6 - raw_value   (apply BEFORE averaging, on the 1-5 coded scale)
scoring_rules.composite_formula: construct_score = mean(the 5 item values for that construct, after reverse-scoring the one reverse-worded item)

MMR.instrument_source: Adapted from Schraw & Dennison (1994) Metacognitive Awareness Inventory

items.wording: I know what method or steps I am following while working on a task.
I am aware of which topics I understand well and which I find difficult.
I notice when I do not understand something during a task.
I can tell when I understand something well enough to explain it to someone else.
I usually don't realise I have misunderstood something until later.
When doing academic work, how often do you complete an academic task entirely without using AI tools?
When doing academic work, how often do you use Generative AI tools to plan or structure an assignment or project?
When doing academic work, how often do you use Generative AI tools to write or draft part of an assignment?
When doing academic work, how often do you use Generative AI tools to review, check, or improve work you have already written?
When doing academic work, how often do you use Generative AI tools to solve problems or work through exercises?
I understand the basic principles of how Generative AI tools produce their responses.
I understand that AI tools can produce confident-sounding statements that are false.
I can recognise when an AI-generated response is likely to be inaccurate.
I know how to check whether information from an AI tool is correct.
I find it hard to tell the difference between a good and a poor AI response.

When doing academic work, how often do you look something up using AI rather than trying to recall or work it out yourself (for example, asking AI for a formula, definition, or fact instead of trying to remember it)?
When doing academic work, how often do you ask AI for the answer to a difficult problem before attempting it yourself?
When doing academic work, how often do you let AI organise or structure your ideas rather than working through them yourself?
When doing academic work, how often do you use AI for parts of a task you could have completed on your own?
When doing academic work, how often do you work through a task yourself first, and use AI only afterwards?

When working on academic tasks, how often do you break down complex problems into smaller parts to understand them better (e.g., splitting a big assignment into smaller tasks, or solving a problem step by step)?
When working on academic tasks, how often do you check whether a claim or answer is actually backed by solid evidence, like a textbook, article, or reliable source, before accepting it as true?
When working on academic tasks, how often do you develop your own understanding of a topic rather than simply accepting what you are told?

When working on academic tasks, how often do you consider alternative viewpoints before reaching a conclusion (e.g., seeking opinions from people with different perspectives before making a decision)?
Once you are convinced you have found the right answer, how often do you stop looking for a better one (e.g., not checking a second source once the first one seems to answer the question)?

c11.wording: To confirm you are reading the questions carefully, please select "Disagree" for this statement.

c27.wording: To confirm you are reading the questions carefully, please select "Almost Always" for this statement.

daily_ai_usage_time.header: On average, how much time do you use Generative AI tools for academic work each day?
